instruction: A grand hall housing a room-sized mechanical computer: columns of stacked brass calculation wheels ticking in sequence, camshafts and crank towers, punch-card readers with card stacks, printout scrolls spooling into baskets, clerks' high desks with green lamps, marble floor, gas chandeliers, and waves of motion rippling along the wheel columns as it computes.
user_instruction: Build a single-file three.js scene: Difference Engine Hall. A grand hall housing a room-sized mechanical computer: columns of stacked brass calculation wheels ticking in sequence, camshafts and crank towers, punch-card readers with card stacks, printout scrolls spooling into baskets, clerks' high desks with green lamps, marble floor, gas chandeliers, and waves of motion rippling along the wheel columns as it computes. Style: computational victorian. Entirely procedural geometry and textures (no external assets; canvas-generated textures are allowed). Compose a full environment — ground/backdrop plus several distinct focal structures and rich supporting props — with style-appropriate materials, a deliberate lighting rig with shadows, atmospheric depth (fog or a gradient sky where fitting), and subtle looping animation on at least three elements. Include OrbitControls with gentle auto-rotate, ACES filmic tone mapping, and a seeded PRNG so the layout is reproducible. Target roughly 600-700 lines of well-organized code.
